# Lab 7.2: Scheduled Queries

## What We Are Going to Do
Schedule a daily aggregation that uses `@run_date`, backfill past dates, and add failure notifications.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Create a scheduled query.** Paste this into a new tab:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  @run_date AS run_date,
  status,
  COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders`
WHERE DATE(created_at) = DATE_SUB(@run_date, INTERVAL 1 DAY)
GROUP BY status;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Click **Schedule → Create new scheduled query**:
   - **Name**: `daily_order_status`
   - **Repeats**: Daily, at 02:00 Asia/Kolkata
   - **Destination**: dataset `lab07`, table `order_status_{run_date}`
   - **Write preference**: Overwrite
   - **Notification**: tick **Send email notifications** on failure

2. **[CLI] Create the same kind of schedule with bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq mk --transfer_config --data_source=scheduled_query --target_dataset=lab07 \
  --display_name="daily_revenue_cli" --schedule="every 24 hours" \
  --params='{
    "query": "SELECT @run_date AS run_date, ROUND(SUM(sale_price),2) AS revenue FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` WHERE DATE(created_at) = DATE_SUB(@run_date, INTERVAL 1 DAY)",
    "destination_table_name_template": "daily_revenue",
    "write_disposition": "WRITE_APPEND"
  }'
bq ls --transfer_config --transfer_location=us</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[CLI] Backfill the last 3 days.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CONFIG=$(bq ls --transfer_config --transfer_location=us --format=json | python3 -c "import sys,json;print([c['name'] for c in json.load(sys.stdin) if c['displayName']=='daily_revenue_cli'][0])")
bq mk --transfer_run --start_time="$(date -u -d '-3 days' +%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00Z)" \
  --end_time="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00Z)" $CONFIG</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Watch the runs.** Open **Pipelines and connections → Pipelines → daily_revenue_cli**. Three backfill runs appear, each with its own `@run_date`.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| `@run_date` | Each run's logical date |
| `{run_date}` template | One table per day (console schedule) |
| Backfill | Past dates processed on demand |
| Engine | Scheduled queries run on the Data Transfer Service |
